Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 12.09.2024 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/Claimants, challenging the award dated Mac 664 of 2017 30.01.2017 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jashpur, District-Jashpur, CG (for short, 'Claims Tribunal'), in Claim Case- 23 of 2015, whereby learned Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.6,24,400/-
Karma Ram Tirkey vs Pal Singh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39816870/
1 as compensation to the claimants.

entities.text: Karma Ram Tirkey vs Pal Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that the deceased-Ravina Tirkey was going to her village Modapara with her friend Neelam Kumari on a Motorcycle bearing No.CG14-MB3071, being driven by one Hemant Tirkey, father of the deceased.

When they reached near village Modapara, offending vehicle Trailor bearing No.CG04-JB 3282, which was being driven rashly and negligently by its driver and owner NA1 Pal Singh, dashed the Motorcycle, by which the deceased and other rider of Motorcycle fell down.
During treatment, the deceased died.
3. Claimants have filed their claim application with the pleading that the deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of accident, and was a student of Class XII.
She was meritorious student, having bright future.
She would have employed in any higher administrative post, and therefore, they have claimed Rs.27,25,000/-, as compensation on various heads.
4. NA1, Owner and Driver of the offending vehicle contested the claim of the claimants and pleaded that the accident was occurred by the negligent driving of the rider of the Motor Cycle.
It is head on collision, and therefore, claimants are not entitled for any compensation.

In alternative, he pleaded that even if the claimants are entitled for Mac 664 of 2017 compensation, since the offending vehicle was duly insured with the Insurance Company, and the driver was having valid and effective driving license with him at the time of accident, liability to pay compensation is upon the Insurance Company.
5. NA2, Insurance Company has also filed its written statement and denied the claim of the claimants, and pleaded that on the date of accident, driver of the offending vehicle was not having any valid and effective driving license with him.

The offending vehicle was being plied without any valid permit or fitness certificate, and the deceased herself was travelling triplet on the Motorcycle,
and therefore, they themselves dashed with the offending vehicle, and therefore, the claim application is liable to be dismissed.

6. NA3 and NA4 also contested the claim, and submitted that after seeing the offending vehicle coming from opposite side rashly and negligently, he stopped his Motorcycle on the side of road, but the offending vehicle dashed the Motorcycle, and therefore, claim application against them is liable to be dismissed.
7. Based on the pleadings made by the respective parties, learned Claims Tribunal has framed 10 issues.

After recording the evidence of the parties and hearing them, passed the award of Rs.6,24,400/- in favour of the claimants as compensation, and the Insurance Company has been exonerated from its liability to pay compensation, and the Mac 664 of 2017 liability to pay compensation is imposed upon the NA1 Pal Singh, owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants would submit that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding less amount towards compensation.
Learned Claims Tribunal has considered monthly income of the deceased as Rs,4,600/-, whereas, it should have taken minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident for assessing the compensation.

He would further submit that future prospects Karma Ram Tirkey vs Pal Singh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39816870/
2 have also not been awarded by the Claims Tribunal, and less amount has been awarded on other conventional heads.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation amount may be enhanced suitably.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for NA2, Insurance Company would support the impugned award and submitted that the Insurance Company has been exonerated in the case, and liability is fastened upon the owner of the vehicle, which is just and proper.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and considered the rival submissions, and perused the record.
11. No document with regard to profession or income of the deceased has been filed.

It is pleaded in the claim application that the deceased was aged about 18 years, and was student of Class XII,
however, no document of her educational qualification has been filed by the claimants.
Mac 664 of 2017 12.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as also pleadings made by learned counsel for the parties, learned Claims Tribunals as considered Rs.4,600/- per month as the monthly income of the deceased, though the minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident prescribed Rs.5,167/-, yet this Court is unable to differ from the consideration of learned Claims Tribunal and approves the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4,600/-, as taken by the learned Claims Tribunal.

13. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:
Notional income of the claimant is being taken as Rs.4,600/- per month.
By adding 40% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.6,440- {4600 + (4600 x 40/100)}.

sentences.text: Out of the above monthly income, half () to be deducted towards personal expenditure of the deceased, as the deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.
Now actual monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.3,220/- {6440  (6440 x 1/2)}.

Actual yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.38,640/- (3220 x 12) Deceased was aged about 20 years at the time of accident and the accident is of the year 2017,
therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma (supra), multiplier of 18 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.6,95,520/- (38640 x 18).
Karma Ram Tirkey vs Pal Singh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39816870/
3 Mac 664 of 2017 Rs.80,000/- towards filial consortium, Funeral expenses-15,000/-,
Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/- in view of the case of Nanu Ram (supra), and 10%
enhancement of the same in every three years comes to Rs.1,32,000/- {80000 +
15000 + 15000 + 22,000 (110000x 20/100)}.

Now total compensation comes to Rs.8,27,520/- (695520 + 132000)
14.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.6,24,400/- already awarded by the Tribunal is now enhanced to Rs.8,27,520/-.
Thereby, the claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.2,03,120/- (827520  624400).
Additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.

15. Since the Insurance Company has been exonerated from its liability to pay compensation on the ground that the policy submitted by the owner of the offending vehicle was found fake, and the liability was fastened upon the owner of the offending vehicle to pay compensation.
Since the Insurance Policy is found to be fake, 'Pay and recover' order cannot be made.

From the record it does not appear that the owner has challenged the impugned award, therefore, the liability to pay compensation is against the owner of the offending vehicle, NA1 Pal Singh is remained intact.
16. Appeal is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above.
17. No order as to costs.

Sd/-
